items.title: Pete Barbutti interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 8, 2022
items.q: Nat said, “You’ve got to hear this guitar player.” And he put this record on, I says, “Wow, who is that?” He said, “Some guy named Joe Pass.”

ctx.x: And they were all very good players. Anyway when this group broke up we added another guitar player from the hometown but he was a pain in the neck and he was sort of a prima donna and that didn’t last long. So then we added two more guys and it just never felt right. So finally the group broke up and I had a chance to reorganize it so I got a trombone player from Scranton, Tony Ardito, he was a great player, and a guitar player from Coatesville, Pennsylvania that we had never heard before but he had a good name,…

always getting in trouble because he’d go in the boiler room and smoke a joint and it would get into the ventilator. People would smell this weird smell. So Lee Dear was the man’s name I can tell you, he’s since passed away, he was a dear man. And he said to Charlie Parker, “You’ve got to get out of here, go to New York.” He later saved the life of maybe the best guitar player who ever lived, Joe Pass, who was a terrible user of hard drugs. And he took Joe Pass physically by the hand, took him out to the airport…
